abstract: Neural posterior estimation (NPE) is a popular Bayesian simulation-based inference (SBI) approach that uses neural networks trained on simulated data--parameter pairs to approximate the posterior given a user-chosen prior. For high-dimensional observations, NPE methods typically approximate the conditional density of the parameter given a user-chosen or learned summary statistic, rather than the entire dataset, due to the curse of dimensionality. However, both approaches face challenges: hand-crafting good summaries for complex models requires considerable effort from scientists, while learning them from massive datasets can be prohibitively computationally expensive. To address these challenges, we propose approximating the conditional density of a parameter given low-dimensional sketches of the data. We show that, for a model with a $p$-dimensional parameter, only $2p+1$ random sketches are needed for posterior consistency. We compare with state-of-the-art embedding networks for NPE, and we find that our method \emph{matches} the best embedding network's performance while \emph{increasing computational efficiency}.

title: Compressed Simulation-Based Inference: Neural Posterior Estimation for Massive Data via Low-Dimensional Sketches
